title: Exception-driven access routing and priority encoder for admin & org requests
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a mix of admin and access requests (RBAC changes, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning, org policy exceptions). The current linear queue treats most as identical tickets causing long resolution paths, missed SLAs for high-risk changes, and unclear handoffs between PM, Security, and SRE.

Goal: Define an "exception-driven priority encoder" that computes a deterministic priority score and recommended routing for each incoming admin/access request. The encoder will annotate tickets with (1) recommended SLA, (2) owning team/role, (3) automation opportunity, and (4) required approvals. This enables faster routing, predictable SLAs, and better metrics for enterprise customers.

Scope: Non-bug requests only (configuration, onboarding, entitlement changes, role templates, SCIM connectors, SSO/SAML integrations, org policy exceptions). Excludes incident response and production outages. Initial rollout will cover self-serve form intake, email intake to enterprise-ops, and manual triage by Solutions Engineering.

Why different: Instead of a fixed gating rubric, this encoder is "exception-driven" — a request's metadata (source, requested scope, platform impact, compliance flags) flips certain rules and escalates otherwise low-priority items when they cross defined exception thresholds (e.g., cross-tenant role creation, granting super-admin to external contractor, changes tied to compliance audits). The model is deterministic, explainable, and easily tuned by policy weights.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New intake form emits normalized request payload with required fields and a computed priority_score
2) Tickets created with priority_score in Linear and an annotation field: recommended_team, recommended_SLA, automation_flag
3) Routing rules in place for top-3 priority buckets that automatically assign to the correct owner queues
4) Dashboard widget showing distribution of request types, avg time-to-resolution by priority bucket, and SLA compliance
5) Security sign-off completed for scoring weights and data fields used (no PII in scoring payload)
tasks: Draft encoder scoring spec and weight table
Design intake form schema + required fields for encoding
Implement Linear ticket annotation payload (API contract)
Build simple rules engine prototype in Console to compute routing
Instrument dashboard metrics and alerts for SLA misses
Run 4-week pilot with 3 enterprise customers and iterate

2026-02-22 - Priya Patel: Drafted scoring table proposal. Proposed features for score: blast_radius (0-5), customer_tier (0-3), automation_fit (0-3, inverted), compliance_flag (0/2), requester_provenance (0-2). Initial weightings suggested; posted in Drive link.

2026-02-25 - Security (Aisha Khan): Reviewed scoring fields. Approved use of flags but requested that exact role names not be stored in encoder payload. Need to ensure KMS-protected fields are used for sensitive fields.

2026-03-05 - Design (Lina Torres): Mocked new intake form and Linear ticket template. Emphasized clear requester guidance to reduce missing fields (SSO metadata, expected end-date, justification).
